$comment: ACKNOWLEDGED findings for rendered-storage-claims.ts.
WHAT AN ENTRY IS. Not a suppression -- a dated, keyed, reasoned record that a finding is
TRUE and is not being fixed in the change that discovered it. Every acknowledged finding is
still counted in the totals the report prints; what the entry buys is a non-red gate, never
a smaller number.
KEYED BY IDENTITY, NEVER BY LINE. `key` is the finding's own stable identity (claim id, or
app + rendered PVC name). A file that grows a line cannot silently re-arm or re-suppress a
different defect.
`observed` PINS WHAT WAS ACKNOWLEDGED. It is compared byte-for-byte against the live finding.
If hindsight starts rendering 12Gi instead of 8Gi, this entry stops covering it and the gate
goes red -- because what was excused was a specific measured defect, not a name. A baseline
that keeps matching after the thing it excused has moved is the vacuity class with a filename.
`liftsWhen` IS REQUIRED. An acknowledgement with no stated exit is a permanent exemption
wearing a temporary word, and the loader refuses one without it.
STALE ENTRIES FAIL. An entry matching nothing is a claim about the tree that stopped being
true, and it is refused exactly like a catalogue row matching no claim.
TWO KINDS OF ENTRY LIVE HERE, and the difference is which list they are in.
`findings` are claims about STORAGE that were measured and are open. hindsight (2 entries)
and nats (1) are inert `valuesObject` paths -- declarations that never reach the chart --
each with an exact one-line fix named in its reason. arc-runner-set/model-cache is a
declared 100 GiB that renders nothing, because the manifest declaring it is orphaned. The
18 `undeclared` entries are PVCs on the non-longhorn class the ladder does not claim to
govern; they are listed with their sizes so the 277 GiB they represent is never invisible.
`unrenderable` are claims about APPS THE CHECKER COULD NOT LOOK AT AT ALL, which is a
strictly worse state than any finding: a finding is a measured disagreement, an unrenderable
app is 0 bytes of evidence. It went from five entries to one on 2026-08-21. The four that
left were every one of them a DEFECT IN OUR OWN MANIFEST -- headscale mounted its declared
volume at a path the chart never writes to and omitted the accessMode the chart requires; oz
pinned a chart version no registry has ever served, which was in turn masking a missing
`clientApi.advertisedHost` and an `adminSecret:` block the chart has no key for; gitlab was
missing the one `configureCertmanager` value its own sibling in infra/ already carried; and
arc-runner-set, the `lookup` one that looked like a limit of the tool, turned out to ship an
explicit escape hatch its own error message recommends. None of the four was a checker
artefact. Every one of them would have failed inside ArgoCD in exactly the same place.
`observed` IS LOAD-BEARING ON BOTH LISTS AS OF 2026-08-21, and it was not before. On
`unrenderable` it pins the FAILURE CLASS -- `helm-pull-failed` (the pin names nothing
upstream serves) versus `helm-template-failed` (the chart is there, our values are wrong) --
and an entry stops covering an app whose class changes. Until then the field was required,
written, and read by nothing, so an acknowledgement about a bad pin would have gone on
silently covering a completely different defect once the pin was fixed. A stale entry on
this list now fails too: an app that started rendering leaves behind a claim about the tree
that has stopped being true, and four such entries would have been left behind by this very
change if nothing required otherwise. Both are enforced by `adjudicateUnrenderable`.
WHAT IS NOT HERE, deliberately: a `structurally-unrenderable` class. It was considered --
a chart that calls `lookup` genuinely cannot be answered offline, and recording that as a
limit of the tool rather than as a defect would be the honest thing IF an app were in it.
Measurement says none is. Creating the class anyway, with no member, would be a category
that cannot fail, which is the thing this whole file refuses. The distinction is carried by
the reason codes instead, where it is checked.

findings.reason: Same root cause as `size full-ai-cluster/hindsight/postgres`, and the more serious half: with `postgresql.primary.persistence.storageClass` inert, the template's `if .Values.postgresql.persistence.storageClass` guard is false and NO storageClassName is emitted, so the volume binds the cluster default `zeta-local-path` -- `rancher.io/local-path` with `reclaimPolicy: Delete`. The semantic-memory Postgres is on node-local storage with a delete reclaim policy, not on replicated longhorn as declared.
findings.liftsWhen: the Application drops the `.primary` level so `postgresql.persistence.storageClass: longhorn` reaches the template
findings.observed: declares storageClass "longhorn", but data/hindsight-postgresql renders NO storageClassName, so it binds the cluster default "zeta-local-path" — a different disk, and on a Delete-reclaim local class a different durability

findings.reason: MEASURED DEFECT, AND THE FIRST TIME IT COULD BE MEASURED AT ALL. gha-runner-scale-set 0.12.1 renders a ServiceAccount, a Role, a RoleBinding and one AutoscalingRunnerSet -- and NO PersistentVolumeClaim. The 100 GiB `arc-model-cache` claim lives in a hand-written manifest, full-ai-cluster/k8s/applications/arc-runner-set/model-cache-pvc.yaml, that NO Application applies: the root App-of-Apps includes only '{*/Application.yaml,Application.yaml}', and arc-runner-set/Application.yaml sources a REMOTE chart, so it cannot apply its own sibling file. The catalogue's own bringUpNote has said this since it was written; what is new is that the CHECKER now says it too, out of the render, instead of being unable to look. Until today this app was UNRENDERABLE (its chart calls `lookup` to discover the controller ServiceAccount), so the single largest row in the ladder was reported as unchecked -- and unchecked hid the fact that it is also wrong. The consequence is not only accounting: the Application ships minRunners: 1 mounting claimName arc-model-cache, so the warm runner stays Pending on a PVC that does not exist. NOT repaired here, because the repair is a decision between two different fixes (add a git-path Application for the PVC, or move the claim into a volumeClaimTemplate) and neither belongs inside the change that made it visible.
findings.liftsWhen: an Application actually applies model-cache-pvc.yaml (a sibling git-path Application, or a root include that reaches it), so `arc-model-cache` appears in the render -- OR the row is retired along with the orphaned manifest, and the 100 GiB leaves the ladder honestly instead of by omission
findings.observed: declares 100Gi on "longhorn" x1 pods, but rendering full-ai-cluster/arc-runner-set produces NO PersistentVolumeClaim matching /^arc-model-cache$/ — the row governs a path that does not exist, and its 100 GiB are counted against nothing

findings.reason: MEASURED DEFECT. The Application sets a TOP-LEVEL `cluster: {enabled: true, replicas: 3}`, but nats chart 1.2.7 reads `config.cluster` (values.yaml:50-55); there is no top-level `cluster` key in the chart at all. The block is inert, the StatefulSet renders `replicas: 1`, and the cluster runs a SINGLE-NODE JetStream. The catalogue row's own `consequence` text asserts the opposite -- that `measured` keeps the quorum and R3 streams still create. It does not: a stream with replicas > 1 refuses to create today. Storage-wise the row over-counts by 20 GiB; the HA claim is the bigger error and is why this is reported rather than silently repaired inside a checker PR.
findings.liftsWhen: the Application moves the `cluster:` block under `config:` and the render shows replicas: 3 (which ADDS 20 GiB of longhorn and two pods -- an operator decision, not a lint fix)
findings.observed: declares 3 pod(s), but the chart renders 1 (nats-js/nats x1) — a claim's cost is size x pod count, so the total is off by -20 GiB

findings.reason: MEASURED DEFECT, NOT AN EXEMPTION FROM ONE. hindsight chart 0.3.0 ships its own hand-rolled postgresql StatefulSet (templates/postgresql-statefulset.yaml:69) reading `postgresql.persistence.size` / `postgresql.persistence.storageClass`. The Application writes `postgresql.PRIMARY.persistence.*` -- the bitnami subchart layout, which this chart does not use -- so both values are inert and the chart default 8Gi renders instead. First measured by PR #13410; this entry records that the fix is a manifest change with real cluster consequences (+2 GiB and a move from the Delete-reclaim local class to longhorn) and is deliberately NOT bundled into the PR that added the checker.
findings.liftsWhen: the Application drops the `.primary` level (or the row is corrected to 8Gi), and the render agrees
findings.observed: declares 10Gi, but the chart renders 8Gi at data/hindsight-postgresql — the declared number never reaches the PVC

findings.reason: OUT OF THE LADDER'S DECLARED SCOPE, AND THE SCOPE IS NOW MEASURABLY UNDER-STATED. storage-profiles.json says 'one row per `longhorn` PVC claim in the tree', and this claim lands on `zeta-local-path` -- the cluster default StorageClass (full-ai-cluster/nixos/modules/local-storage.nix), a node-local hostPath class with reclaimPolicy: Delete. It is still real disk on the box being provisioned, so it is recorded here rather than filtered out: the rendered zeta-local-path total is 277 GiB (201 in full-ai-cluster, 76 in the infra tree) against the 103 GiB that single-node-budget.json's $comment_nodeDiskGib records. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-21: it was 201 GiB until full-ai-cluster/gitlab became renderable, at which point 76 GiB that had been invisible-because-unrenderable turned into 76 GiB that is merely undeclared. The disk did not grow; the count did.
findings.liftsWhen: the catalogue grows rows for the non-longhorn class, OR single-node-budget.json's zeta-local-path figure is re-derived from this render; either way this entry stops matching and fails as stale
findings.observed: the chart renders a PersistentVolumeClaim of 1Gi x1 on "zeta-local-path" (no storageClassName; cluster default) that NO catalogue row covers — 1 GiB of real disk that no profile total includes

findings.reason: OUT OF THE LADDER'S DECLARED SCOPE, AND NEWLY VISIBLE RATHER THAN NEWLY REAL. This PVC has always been what full-ai-cluster/gitlab provisions; until 2026-08-21 the app would not template at all (it lacked `global.ingress.configureCertmanager: false`), so the checker reported it as UNRENDERABLE and counted its disk as neither verified nor refuted. Supplying that one value moved these 76 GiB from unchecked to undeclared, which is a worse-looking gate and a strictly better ledger. Same class as the sibling infra/gitlab entries and identical in size, because it is the same chart at the same pin: the rendered zeta-local-path total is 277 GiB (201 in full-ai-cluster, 76 in the infra tree) against the 103 GiB that single-node-budget.json's $comment_nodeDiskGib records. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-21: it was 201 GiB until full-ai-cluster/gitlab became renderable, at which point 76 GiB that had been invisible-because-unrenderable turned into 76 GiB that is merely undeclared. It is still real disk on the box being provisioned, so it is recorded here rather than filtered out: the rendered zeta-local-path total is 277 GiB (201 in full-ai-cluster, 76 in the infra tree) against the 103 GiB that single-node-budget.json's $comment_nodeDiskGib records. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-21: it was 201 GiB until full-ai-cluster/gitlab became renderable, at which point 76 GiB that had been invisible-because-unrenderable turned into 76 GiB that is merely undeclared. The disk did not grow; the count did.
findings.liftsWhen: the catalogue grows rows for the non-longhorn class, OR single-node-budget.json's zeta-local-path figure is re-derived from this render; either way this entry stops matching and fails as stale
